Antarctica New Zealand

Antarctica New Zealand is the government agency responsible for carrying out New Zealand's activities in Antarctica, supporting world leading science and environmental protection. Our vision is: Antarctica and the Southern Ocean – valued, protected, understood.

Webinar: NZ ETS unit limits and price control settings 2026–2030 (8 May 2025)

Each year, the Climate Change Commission provides advice on the New Zealand Emissions Trading Scheme (NZ ETS) unit limits and price control settings. In this webinar, Chief Executive Jo Hendy and Principal Analysts Eva Murray and Matthew Smith provide a high-level overview of the Commission’s latest advice on the NZ ETS, including insights about this year’s recommendations.

Read the full report and find more information on our website: https://www.climatecommission.govt.nz/our-work/advice-to-government-topic/nz-ets/our-advice-on-the-nz-ets/nz-ets-2026-2030/


CHAPTERS:

00:00 Welcome - Sally Garden, Project Director

01:46 Overview - Jo Hendy, Chief Executive
03:50 How the NZ ETS works | Context: Approach to managing NZ ETS settings
06:30 Context: wider issues
09:00 Context: Framework in the Climate Change Response Act

Unit limits - Matt Smith, Principal Advisor
10:42 Our advice
12:38 The Government's second emissions reduction plan
14:20 The established 7-step method
16:25 Surplus volume is lower than previous forecast

Price control settings - Eva Murray, Principal Advisor
18:19 Fit for purpose with inflation adjustment
20:50 ERP2 means reassessment needed
22:23 Consistency with the second emissions budget
24:20 Consistency with third budget and NDC

27:55 Next steps - Jo Hendy, Chief Executive

Q&A
29:23 What does global uncertainty, following the US leaving the Paris Agreement, mean for the NZ ETS?
33:00 What evidence is there for saying it's viable for the Government to meet its nationally determined contribution (NDC)?
35:50 Given the Commission previously forecast a huge surplus of units, how can we have  confidence in this report forecasting of a deficit?
36:58 Role of forestry in offsetting emissions
39:00 Release of additional units in years 3–5 in this advice
42:15 Future work that might narrow the uncertainty range
44:35 How do you ensure forestry offsets and overseas mitigation do not delay investment in decarbonising the NZ economy?
45:47 How is the impact of the current government's policies reflected in this advice?
48:35 Risks of wildfire on forestry's impact and permanence
51:25 Biodiversity impact of afforestation from exotic forestry
53:51 Should we ease off the NZ ETS given current economic pressures on communities?

Hāngī safety with Ozzy

Former All Black and Māori All Black Glen Osborne shares our safety tips for hāngī, umu, lovo or braai.
Before you light, always check the local Fire Danger at www.checkitsalright.nz. If the local fire Danger is High, Very High or Extreme, don't light. If the Fire Season is Restricted, you will need a permit to have a beach bonfire. If the Fire Season is Prohibited, there is a total fire ban in place. Also remember to check the local council rules, there are often total fire bans on beach areas.

Graduate Stories: La Rochelle Bernstein

Back in South Africa 🇿🇦, La Rochelle was raised in a multi-racial household. It is in this upbringing and her passion for teaching that pushed her to pursue a degree in education. Now a teacher 👩‍🏫  with an even wider perspective, she is now teaching young students the value of diversity and inclusion, helping raise a new generation to be curious and respectful of other cultures.

Graduate Stories: Marcel Teraimana

Despite a series of personal challenges, Marcel forged on to finish his course thanks to his determination, his friends, and the help of his lecturers who went above and beyond their work hours to help him and his classmates to be in a position to succeed. Now, he’s paying it forward as he is now the one guiding learners as a student life guide. Talk about a full circle moment. 🧑‍🎓👩‍🎓 💖  
 
#GraduationWeek
#AchievementUnlocked
#GetMoreYourYourFuture

Graduate Stories: Nick Odhiambo

From Kenya to New Zealand 🇰🇪✈️🇳🇿
 
After several degrees and work stints from different countries, Nick hit a plateau in his life and career. So when he and his wife made the move to New Zealand, he decided to realign his skills and enrolled at MIT not just once but twice. He felt like he was guided by his course to being prepared and well-equipped the moment he stepped out of school. Now he is working as an engineer and has made Aotearoa as his permanent home.

Tuku Taonga Celebration 2025

“Life is a journey. Education is a journey.” 🧑🎓 👩🎓

This was the message that filled the Marae as we celebrated our Māori ākonga (students) on achieving a significant milestone - graduation. In an educational journey filled with bumpy roads and joyous trails, no graduate carried on alone. Pouako (teachers), whānau and friends were there to support and uplift them, not just with each step forward but also during setbacks.
 
#Whakamihi 
#MahiTikaAna
#GraduationWeek
#TukuTaonga
#GetMoreYourYourFuture

Graduate Stories: Sione Fakahau

No matter the age, education is for everyone. 💯

These words hold true to our graduate, Sione. He finished high school in 1992 and for the next twenty eight years, Sione and his family persevered through hardship and poverty. So when the opportunity for education came knocking, even after almost three decades, he made the most out of it. 

While it was hard, his community made the journey worthwhile. As his way of giving back, he now serves as a navigator for families who are still finding their path.

Celebrating New Zealand Sign Language Week

We are celebrating a beautiful language with week, New Zealand Sign Language. 👍 ✌️ ✋ 
 
Prakashni, one of our students here at MIT, is among us in spreading awareness of New Zealand Sign Language. In this yearly celebration, we stand proudly in unity with Prakashni and the thousands of deaf people in Aotearoa.
 
#NZSLweek
#DeafAotearoa
#Inclusion
